pr.title: Leave a thread the pull request's author resolved for its owner to decide
pr.head: 50579a8a42f67f2c7939e3e21f1bec1ee5b8e86d

summary: A Projector review leaves finding threads on a pull request: inline comments that carry a hidden projector-finding marker. On every later head the reviewer checks each one and settles it with project review settle, which posts a reply and resolves or unresolves the thread. Until now the reviewer's word was final, so it could reopen a thread that anyone had resolved.

That was wrong on another person's pull request. When the author resolved a finding thread there, often after declining the finding, the reviewer reopened it. The reviewer does not own the merge, so it was overriding the owner's decision about their own change.

This pull request makes settle --result reopened refuse when the pull request's author resolved the thread and the author is not the reviewer. The refusal names both owner decisions: when the owner declined the finding, name it in the review body as declined, and when a claimed fix does not hold, post a new finding. census --json now names the pull request's author and each thread's resolved_by, so the reviewer sees an overruled thread before it tries to reopen it. The review-pr skill adds an Overruled case that says the same. A self-review, where the author is the reviewer, behaves as before.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Self-review: the reviewer's account wrote the pull request.
  • Cross-author review: someone else wrote it, such as a person's pull request that the CI bot reviews.
  • Settle: reply on a finding thread with a verify marker and set it resolved or open.
  • Overruled: the new case, where the author resolved the thread on their own pull request.

cards.title: What the review flagged
cards.html: The review of this head is clean. An earlier review found that the refusal told the reviewer to record a finding as declined even when the author had resolved it after a fix that does not hold. The refusal now names both cases, so that finding is fixed. The review lists two suggestions: have fix-pr treat a new finding on code it already fixed as a recurrence, and rewrap one long line in review-pr.

groups.title: The refusal in settle
groups.kicker: How settle and census tell an owner's resolution from any other
intro: settle already reads the thread from GitHub before it changes anything, to check that the thread is a Projector finding on this pull request. That query now also asks for resolvedBy, the login that resolved the thread, and the pull request's author. census asks for the same two fields and returns them in --json.

The new overruled function is true when the thread is resolved, the resolver is the author, and the author is not the reviewer. It compares logins without regard to case. settle checks it only for --result reopened, and raises before it takes a token or posts anything. The message tells the reviewer what to do for a declined finding and for a fix that does not hold.

files.note: Both thread queries gain resolvedBy and the pull request's author, census and finding_thread return them, and settle refuses an overruled reopen.

checks.text: The refusal runs before reviewer_token and before any mutation, so a refused reopen posts no reply. test_refuses_to_reopen_a_thread_another_author_resolved_on_their_pull_request asserts no mutation ran, and it passed on this head.

files.note: The fake GraphQL nodes gain resolvedBy and the pull request's author. New tests cover the census fields, a refused reopen with both halves of its message, and the three reopens that still work.

groups.title: The skills and documentation
groups.kicker: What the reviewer and the author are told to do now
intro: review-pr no longer calls the reviewer's resolution final in every case, and adds the Overruled bullet beside Fixed, Accepted, Kept, and Reopened. fix-pr tells the author what to expect on a pull request another login reviews: the reviewer leaves the author's resolved threads alone, and a new finding on code the author already fixed counts as a recurrence, so fix-pr stops and reports it. docs/cli.md lists the new refusal, and docs/plugins.md says the same in its overview.

checks.text: fix-pr resolves a thread once it pushes a fix, so on a cross-author pull request most author-resolved threads claim a fix, not a decline. The skill tells the two apart by reading the author's replies.

files.note: The Verify earlier findings section gains the Overruled case, and says that census --json names who resolved each thread.
Tells the author that the reviewer leaves a thread the author resolved alone, and that a new finding on code the author already fixed is a recurrence: stop and report it rather than fixing it again.
Documents the new census --json fields and the new settle refusal.
